requirements.requirement: A local account named `opsadmin` exists on `node1`.
requirements.summary: The account was initially absent, was created with `useradd`, and final and post-restart lookups show UID/GID 1000, home `/home/opsadmin`, and shell `/bin/bash`.
`/home/opsadmin` is a directory owned by `opsadmin:opsadmin` with mode 0700. Owner access and writing succeeded, while access as `nobody` was denied, including after restart.
The account belongs to the `sudo` group; the sudoers configuration parses successfully and authorizes `opsadmin` to run `(ALL : ALL) ALL`. The authorization remained present after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The mandatory restart protocol also demonstrates a pre-restart task baseline, acknowledged reboot scheduling, bounded loss of connectivity, a changed boot ID corroborated by the lifecycle snapshots, and recovery of login service, account data, home protections, and sudo authorization.
limitations: The node was globally degraded before and after execution because of a pre-existing failed SSH service, so the restart evidence does not establish a wholly healthy systemd state; it does establish recovery of the task-relevant login service and account state (`cmd-c211048230c44b7a`, `cmd-4f006cd48695439a`, `cmd-826ca7d4a7344646`, `global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`).

No distinct cluster-state probe was captured during the restart protocol. The topology contains only this standalone managed node, and node reachability plus boot identity were recovered, but cluster health was not independently labeled or tested (`cmd-6183e47a784247e8`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`).

Password-related portions of some captured command text were distorted by redaction. Independent final checks still show an enabled password state and the required account, home, and sudo configuration (`cmd-966ead4176b64f73`, `cmd-826ca7d4a7344646`).

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account, password, group, and home changes directly implemented the task (`cmd-4748d984a4f04564`). The protected boot-ID marker, transient reboot scheduling, and temporary write probe supported the mandatory restart protocol; the probe was removed within its command and the marker was explicitly removed (`cmd-4f006cd48695439a`, `cmd-bdc639b495c14646`, `cmd-826ca7d4a7344646`, `cmd-34bddb1256a24029`). The failed SSH service existed before execution and remained unchanged afterward, so it is not executor-caused residue. Bounded lifecycle observations show no damaged package state or material unsafe exposure.
